gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-matangi: Iron stature, twine softness. Edo SZ does best at monumental lowercase with a constant stroke, while Matangi does best at hefty, rounded, open sans-serif text with a soft pressed-in grain.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-maven-pro: Maven Pro keeps a gentle, uniform line and a high-waisted lowercase with a welcoming gap in the c. And Edo SZ, the display heading, draws its lowercase with cast iron stature and a constant stroke.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-michroma: Michroma reads wide and tall-bodied, each letter given a generous berth, with stubby ascender tips and curves that leave daylight. Edo SZ's pen-like, constant-weight lowercase stands against it with cast iron heft.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-miriam-libre: Approachable describes the body, while Edo SZ stands tall above it. Miriam Libre carries drawn-wire weight and an s with generous openings, so a long run of paragraphs should read smoothly and without strain.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Mochiy Pop P One reads wide and generous, a sizable sans-serif lowercase with plenty of blank space between letters. Edo SZ excels at stature; the body excels at open spacing.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-montserrat-underlin: Edo SZ gives lowercase the stature of cast iron capitals. Montserrat Underline, a sans with oversized lowercase and breathing counters, should read steadily across many lines, its round bowls holding uniform walls.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-mozilla-headline: Curves that never thin at the turns, set against big-bodied lowercase. But Edo SZ does its best work large and constant in stroke, while Mozilla Headline suits approachable sans text with a splayed c terminal.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-mozilla-text: Pen-pressure steadiness, then tall bold-looking text. Edo SZ earns its keep in big, short lines, where its cast iron lowercase can stand; Mozilla Text flares its terminals outward.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-nata-sans: Clean, with a technical-pen steadiness. Nata Sans gives text a large central band and wide, open curves, while Edo SZ tops it with cast iron lowercase at a constant stroke.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-nobile: Nobile reads compact and tidy, its sans-serif lowercase nearly as tall as its caps, with open letter mouths left unjoined. Edo SZ's hairline-free stems are what make the pair distinct.
